result:
All done — `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` passes (7 tests across 3 files, including the 4 new ones).

I added `app/Http/Middleware/ThrottleLoginMiddleware.ts`, which builds the limiter from Guren's own `createRateLimitMiddleware` (re-exported by `@guren/core`) configured for 5 requests per 60 s against a dedicated in-process `MemoryRateLimitStore` under a `login:` key prefix, and wired it onto the login submission only in `routes/auth.ts:11` (`guest.post('/login', [LoginController, 'store'], ThrottleLoginMiddleware)`), so `GET /login`, registration, and every other route are untouched. `trustProxy` is left at its default of `false`, so the client identity is the socket peer address that `bin/serve.ts` exposes via `ctx.env.server.requestIP()` — forwarded-for style headers are ignored, and when no address can be resolved the framework falls back to a single shared per-route bucket, which counts the request rather than letting it through. Counting happens before the controller runs, so every submission counts whether the credentials were right or wrong, and the 6th within the window gets a 429 with a `Retry-After` header (in seconds) instead of reaching `LoginController.store`. Tests live in `tests/LoginThrottle.test.ts` and cover the 6th-submission 429 plus `Retry-After`, a correct login still redirecting to `/dashboard` within the limit, a correct login refused with 429 once throttled, spoofed `X-Forwarded-For` values not buying a fresh budget, and `GET /login` and `/` staying reachable while throttled; the store is exported so those tests can clear the counters between cases.
